title: Nightcap prefill & kernel sync — standup summary
content:
Context
Week of 2029-09-16, late-shift synthesis after two overnight runs. This doc captures the informal standup and the experimental notes from the night team focused on prefill/prefetch behavior, kernel handshake timing, and micro-batch assembly heuristics. Intended as a single-pane capture for next-day sync and follow-ups.

Attendees (ad-hoc nightcap):
- Priya Menon (owner) — triage + notes
- Ethan Park — kernel changes + perf measurements
- Liam Chen — KV cache heuristics and shadowing
- María Gomez — telemetry + tracing
- Aisha Rahman — canary rollout and safety checks

High-level summary
- Rolled a lightweight kernel handshake delay reduction (tweak: handshake_backoff_ms from 6 -> 3) on two canary hosts for traffic slice 1%.
- Enabled prefill-shadowing for cohort B (10% of requests) to exercise the KV prefill code path without affecting live responses (shadow mode).
- Adjusted micro-batch assembly window from 6ms -> 9ms for low-concurrency probes to reduce small-batch penalties observed in p50.
- Observed a transient p99 latency uptick on canary between 03:20–03:40 UTC; traced to an eviction storm in the prefills (simultaneous TTL expirations).

What changed (technical detail)
1) Kernel handshake backoff reduction (Ethan)
- Rationale: earlier handshake jitter was adding 4–8ms to short requests. Reducing backoff helps hand off warmed kernels faster during low-queue periods.
- Implementation: parameterized handshake_backoff_ms and handshake_retries in runtime config (PR 1427).
- Rollout: canary on two hosts, monitored for error increase and CPU regrowth.
- Early result: p50 latency for short text completion decreased ~2.6ms on canary. No error spike correlated except at the eviction incident window.

2) Prefill shadowing (Liam)
- Rationale: collect prefill hit-rate and eviction behavior under real traffic without making prefills authoritative.
- Behavior: shadow requests run through prefill code path; outcomes logged to new telemetry bucket prefill.shadow.* but not applied to live cache for production routing.
- Observations: shadow cohorts show 16% prefill hit-rate for 1–32 token prompts and 9% for 33–128 tokens. Suggests prefix reuse is concentrated in short queries.

3) Micro-batching window tweak (Priya + Aisha)
- Change: increased assembly window to 9ms for low-QPS backends to allow slight coalescing, while leaving high-QPS pools at 4ms.
- Why: small batches (size 1–2) were dominating cost for a subset of customers; moderate window reduces per-token overhead.
- Tradeoff observed: small bump in tail latency for a handful of long-running interactive sessions. Will monitor.

Telemetry and anomalies (María)
- Incident 03:20–03:40 UTC: p99 jump ~42ms over baseline. Root cause: simultaneous expiry for 1200 prefills (TTL aligned with deploy artifact at 03:00) triggered concurrent repopulation attempts, overlapping with kernel handshake retries.
- Mitigation applied: stagger prefill TTLs by jittering expiry windows in the coordinator (hotfix pushed to night hosts).
- Logs/IDs: trace ids attached to GitHub PR 1427 and INF-4721. Full traces: https://sentry.redwood.ai/serving-runtime/trace/tnk-9f2

Preliminary metrics (night run aggregate)
- Baseline (prior night): p50=14.2ms, p95=62.1ms, p99=113.7ms, throughput=12.9k reqs/min
- Canary (with changes): p50=11.6ms, p95=60.5ms, p99=130.9ms (spike window excluded p99=116ms), throughput ~+1.8%
- Shadow prefill hit rates: short queries (1–32) = 16.1% hit, medium (33–128) = 9.2% hit, long (>128) negligible

Action items (owners + due)
- A1: Liam — implement TTL jitter generator in prefill coordinator and land canary (INF-4725). Due: 2029-09-21.
- A2: Ethan — increase handshake telemetry granularity (include kernel load and CPU steal) and add synthetic low-latency probes. PR: follow-up to 1427. Due: 2029-09-22.
- A3: Priya — prepare short postmortem for 03:20 incident (include trace waterfall + eviction snapshot). Due: 2029-09-20.
- A4: Aisha — run targeted A/B on micro-batching window (9ms vs 6ms) for two customer slices (alpha/beta) and report cost delta. Due: 2029-09-27.
- A5: María — update dashboards to surface prefill.shadow.* metrics and add alert for >1k simultaneous TTL expirations. Due: 2029-09-21.

Open questions / unresolved items
- Q1: Prefill eviction policy — is LFU with age-bias sufficient for workloads with tight prefix reuse, or do we need per-model cohort quotas? (Liam to prototype).
- Q2: How aggressive should handshake_backoff reduction be for multi-tenant hosts with bursty noisy neighbors? Need simulation of burst+coldchain mixing.
- Q3: Should shadow prefill data be used to seed a warm-cache rollout for Dedicated customers (privacy + determinism concerns)? Product/Legal sync required.

Notes to self / night-shift observations
- Shadow logs are very noisy; need a thin sampler to avoid high-ingest cost for telemetry. Suggest 1:10 downsample at ingestion + metadata tagging for reconstruction.
- Several small clients benefit disproportionately from the longer micro-batching window; highlight for cost-ops.
- Handshake change seems net-positive for short completions but exposes eviction interplay; consider handshake gating if prefill queue > X.

Links and references
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1427
- Jira: INF-4721 (prefill eviction incident), INF-4725 (ttl jitter)
- Playbook (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SR/Prefill+Shadowing+Playbook
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime-nightshift (pinned: morning summary)

Next steps / meeting cadence
- Quick sync 2029-09-20 09:00 PDT (standup) to review A1–A3 status and decide whether to expand prefill shadow cohort to 25%.
- If A1 mitigations hold and telemetry looks stable, plan gradual rollout of handshake_backoff reduction to 10% of hosts on 2029-09-24.

End of nightcap notes.
(Informal; will convert to a cleaner handoff for the daytime squad and link PRs + traces in the 09:00 standup.)
